questions.question: A design airplane has a weight of 2,200 lb and a wing area of 90 ft 2 . It is to be certified as acrobatic category under FAR part 23. What is the negative limit maneuvering load factor in which the airplane must be designed for
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 3.0. The supplied key selects 3.0 for the negative acrobatic-category maneuvering factor; the negative sign describes the load direction, while the listed choice gives its magnitude.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• 2.1: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the supplied key selects 3.
• 3.8: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the supplied key selects 3.
• 2.5: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the supplied key selects 3.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Positive and negative load factors act in opposite vertical directions; the source option states only the magnitude.

💡 Memory Hook:
Acrobatic: 3.0 magnitude on the negative side.

🎯 Board Tip:
Check whether the option includes a sign or gives only the factor magnitude.

questions.question: A simply supported beam, 3 meters in length is acted upon by an upward uniformly distributed load along its entire length with a magnitude of 8 KN/m. What is the maximum shear imposed on the beam by the load
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 12 KN. The total uniform load is 8 kN/m ? 3 m = 24 kN. Symmetry places half at each support, so the maximum shear magnitude is 12 kN.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• 24 KN: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the total uniform load is 8 kn/m ? 3 m = 24 kn.
• 6 KN: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the total uniform load is 8 kn/m ? 3 m = 24 kn.
• 8 KN: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the total uniform load is 8 kn/m ? 3 m = 24 kn.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Support reaction is not the same as the total distributed load; shear changes linearly along the beam.

💡 Memory Hook:
Uniform load ? half the total at each support.

🎯 Board Tip:
For a simply supported beam, calculate reactions before reading the shear diagram.

questions.question: A simply supported beam, 3 meters in length is acted upon by an upward uniformly distributed load along it entire length with a magnitude 8 KN/m. What is the maximum bending moment imposed on the beam by the load

• 18 KN - m: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for a simply supported beam with full-span uniform load, mmax = wl?/8 = 8?3?/8 = 9 kn?m.

questions.question: Structural members designed to support loadings applied perpendicular to their axes. They are long, straight bars having a constant cross - sectional area.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Beams. Beams are slender members that primarily carry loads transverse to their longitudinal axis, creating shear and bending.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Shafts: It does not match the condition or structural role described; beams are slender members that primarily carry loads transverse to their longitudinal axis, creating shear and bending.
• Plates: It does not match the condition or structural role described; beams are slender members that primarily carry loads transverse to their longitudinal axis, creating shear and bending.
• Bulkhead: It does not match the condition or structural role described; beams are slender members that primarily carry loads transverse to their longitudinal axis, creating shear and bending.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
A shaft is primarily associated with torsion; a plate is a surface element; a bulkhead is a transverse structural partition.

💡 Memory Hook:
Beam bends; shaft twists.

🎯 Board Tip:
Identify the direction of load relative to the member axis.

questions.question: The test pilot of a design airplane observed that if the airplane is acted upon by a strong updraft, the airplane oscillates vertically. The airplane is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Statically stable. Static stability describes the initial tendency to move back toward equilibrium after a disturbance. The prompt reports an oscillatory response but does not specify whether it damps out.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Dynamically stable: It does not match the condition or structural role described; static stability describes the initial tendency to move back toward equilibrium after a disturbance.
• Statically and dynamically unstable: It does not match the condition or structural role described; static stability describes the initial tendency to move back toward equilibrium after a disturbance.
• Statically and dynamically stable: It does not match the condition or structural role described; static stability describes the initial tendency to move back toward equilibrium after a disturbance.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Dynamic stability concerns how the motion changes with time; oscillation alone does not establish damping.

💡 Memory Hook:
Static = initial response; dynamic = motion over time.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not infer positive dynamic stability from the word oscillates alone.

questions.question: For a given aircraft at a given condition, the limit load is constant. The ultimate load is dictated by the factor of safety. Choose which of the following statements are CORRECT in relation to the factor of safety and ultimate load.
choices: As the factor of safety increases, the ultimate load decreases.
As the ultimate load increases, the factor of safety decreases.
As the factor of safety increases, the ultimate load increases.
The factor of safety is constant at 1.5 therefore, ultimate load is als o constant.
questions.answerText: As the factor of safety increases, the ultimate load increases.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: As the factor of safety increases, the ultimate load increases.. Ultimate load equals limit load multiplied by the factor of safety. With limit load fixed, a larger factor of safety raises ultimate load.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• As the factor of safety increases, the ultimate load decreases.: It does not match the condition or structural role described; ultimate load equals limit load multiplied by the factor of safety.
• As the ultimate load increases, the factor of safety decreases.: It does not match the condition or structural role described; ultimate load equals limit load multiplied by the factor of safety.
• The factor of safety is constant at 1.5 therefore, ultimate load is als o constant.: It does not match the condition or structural role described; ultimate load equals limit load multiplied by the factor of safety.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
The relationship is direct, not inverse; the stated factor is not arbitrary when the certification basis fixes it.

💡 Memory Hook:
Ultimate = limit ? safety factor.

🎯 Board Tip:
Keep limit load and ultimate load distinct.

questions.question: Normally designed to provide restraint against rotation and all translations; therefore, reactive fo rces and moments are developed along the directions where movements are not permitted.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Fixed support. A fixed support restrains translation in both axes and rotation, so it can develop reaction forces and a reaction moment.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Hinge support: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a fixed support restrains translation in both axes and rotation, so it can develop reaction forces and a reaction moment.
• Roller support: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a fixed support restrains translation in both axes and rotation, so it can develop reaction forces and a reaction moment.
• Wedge support: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a fixed support restrains translation in both axes and rotation, so it can develop reaction forces and a reaction moment.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
A hinge permits rotation; a roller permits motion along its surface; neither restrains all three motions.

💡 Memory Hook:
Fixed support blocks motion and rotation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Count permitted degrees of freedom to identify a support.

questions.question: It is a structure composed of slender members joined together at their end points, in which the memb ers are subjected to only axial loads.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Truss structure 2 6. A truss is built from slender members joined at their ends and idealized as carrying axial tension or compression.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Beam structure: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a truss is built from slender members joined at their ends and idealized as carrying axial tension or compression.
• Monocoque structure: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a truss is built from slender members joined at their ends and idealized as carrying axial tension or compression.
• Semi - monocoque structure: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a truss is built from slender members joined at their ends and idealized as carrying axial tension or compression.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Beams carry bending; monocoque and semi-monocoque describe shell-based aircraft construction rather than pin-jointed axial members.

💡 Memory Hook:
Truss members carry axial force.

🎯 Board Tip:
Look for end-jointed members and axial-only loading.

questions.question: Members w hich are loaded so that they are compressed axially and therefore have developed within them compressive resistances or stresses.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Beams. The provided key marks Beams. However, the stem describes members loaded axially in compression, which is the usual definition of columns. This source-key conflict is retained for verification.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Columns: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the provided key marks beams.
• Shafts: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the provided key marks beams.
• Trusses: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the provided key marks beams.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Columns are the compression members described by the stem; beams are normally identified with transverse loading and bending.

💡 Memory Hook:
Column = axial compression; beam = transverse load and bending.

🎯 Board Tip:
Check the marked choice in the supplied answer-key PDF before studying this item.

questions.question: It is a measure of the intensity of load acting on a definite plan e passing throu gh a given point in the material.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Stress. Stress is internal force intensity: the force acting over a unit area at a point or section.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Shear: It does not match the condition or structural role described; stress is internal force intensity: the force acting over a unit area at a point or section.
• Torque: It does not match the condition or structural role described; stress is internal force intensity: the force acting over a unit area at a point or section.
• Strain: It does not match the condition or structural role described; stress is internal force intensity: the force acting over a unit area at a point or section.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Shear and torque are load actions; strain measures deformation, not force per area.

💡 Memory Hook:
Stress = force/area; strain = deformation ratio.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse a load with the material response to that load.

questions.question: The axial strain in a member is always accompanied by a lateral strain of opposite sign. Thus, if a member stretches under load, its cross - sectional area becomes smaller at the sa me time. The relationship of the lateral strain to axial strain is expressed by:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Poisson's Ratio. Poisson's ratio relates lateral strain to axial strain. A member stretched axially contracts laterally, so the strains have opposite signs.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Modulus ratio: It does not match the condition or structural role described; poisson's ratio relates lateral strain to axial strain.
• Stress - strain relationship: It does not match the condition or structural role described; poisson's ratio relates lateral strain to axial strain.
• Hooke's Law: It does not match the condition or structural role described; poisson's ratio relates lateral strain to axial strain.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Hooke's law relates stress and strain in the elastic range; modulus is a stress-to-strain ratio, not the lateral-to-axial ratio.

💡 Memory Hook:
Poisson compares sideways strain with lengthwise strain.

🎯 Board Tip:
Track the direction of each strain and its sign.

questions.question: A transverse load on a member tends to make the member rotate about an axis at a section aw ay from that where the load is applied and normal to the axis of the member. If the member is restrained fro m rotating at any section other than that at which the load is applied, internal tension stresses are set up at one side of the member and compressi on at the other. At any section where such stresses are present the member is said to be subjected to:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Bending. A transverse load creates a bending moment; the section develops tension on one side and compression on the other.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Torsion: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a transverse load creates a bending moment; the section develops tension on one side and compression on the other.
• Shear: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a transverse load creates a bending moment; the section develops tension on one side and compression on the other.
• Compression: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a transverse load creates a bending moment; the section develops tension on one side and compression on the other.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Torsion twists about the member axis; shear tends to slide adjacent portions; pure compression acts along the axis.

💡 Memory Hook:
Bending: tension on one side, compression on the other.

🎯 Board Tip:
A bending section has a neutral axis separating tension and compression.

questions.question: If loads are applied to a member so that it tends to twist about an axis, internal shear stresses ar e s et up in the member at any section between the application of load and the reaction to resist the twisting force. In such a case the member is said to be subjected to:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Torsion. A torque that tends to twist a member produces torsional shear stresses within it.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Shear: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a torque that tends to twist a member produces torsional shear stresses within it.
• Bending: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a torque that tends to twist a member produces torsional shear stresses within it.
• Compression: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a torque that tends to twist a member produces torsional shear stresses within it.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Bending curves the member; direct shear slides one part past another; compression shortens it axially.

💡 Memory Hook:
Torque causes torsion.

🎯 Board Tip:
Follow the direction of the applied moment about the member axis.

questions.question: The ratio of shear stress to strain be low the proportional limit is called shear modulus of elasticity or:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Modulus of rigidity. The shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain in the linear-elastic range.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Poisson's Ratio: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain in the linear-elastic range.
• Stress - strain relationship: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain in the linear-elastic range.
• Modulus ratio: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain in the linear-elastic range.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Poisson's ratio compares lateral and axial strain; Young's modulus is the normal stress-to-strain ratio.

💡 Memory Hook:
G is the elastic modulus for shear.

🎯 Board Tip:
Pair shear stress with shear strain.

questions.question: The total moment due to internal stresses of a shaft or tube is equal in magnitude to the exter nal torque, and is given by the equation dA r L G T 2 . The quantity dA r 2 is known as the:
choices: Moment of inertia about a base
Product of inertia about inclined axis through a centroid
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Polar moment of inertia. In the torsion relation, the area integral of radius squared is the polar moment of inertia, J, which describes resistance to twisting.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Radius of gravitation: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in the torsion relation, the area integral of radius squared is the polar moment of inertia, j, which describes resistance to twisting.
• Moment of inertia about a base: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in the torsion relation, the area integral of radius squared is the polar moment of inertia, j, which describes resistance to twisting.
• Product of inertia about inclined axis through a centroid: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in the torsion relation, the area integral of radius squared is the polar moment of inertia, j, which describes resistance to twisting.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
The other inertia terms describe different axes or mass distribution; the polar moment uses distance squared from the shaft axis.

💡 Memory Hook:
Polar J measures area spread around the shaft axis.

🎯 Board Tip:
Use J for circular-shaft torsion and I for bending.

questions.question: The maximum anticipated loads in the entire service life - span of a flight vehicle is called:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Limit loads. Limit loads are the maximum loads expected in service. Ultimate loads are obtained by applying the required safety factor to limit loads.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Ultimate loads: It does not match the condition or structural role described; limit loads are the maximum loads expected in service.
• Design loads: It does not match the condition or structural role described; limit loads are the maximum loads expected in service.
• Imposed loads: It does not match the condition or structural role described; limit loads are the maximum loads expected in service.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Ultimate load includes the safety factor; design or imposed load are not the defined service maximum in this item.

💡 Memory Hook:
Limit = expected service maximum; ultimate = factored limit.

🎯 Board Tip:
Check whether the question asks expected load or factored strength load.

questions.question: This condition is obtained in a pullout at the highest possible angle of attack o f the wing. The lift and drag forces are perpendicular and parallel respectively to the relative wind.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Positive high angle of attack. A pullout at the wing's highest angle of attack produces positive high-angle-of-attack loading: lift is positive and drag opposes the relative wind.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Positive low angle of attack: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a pullout at the wing's highest angle of attack produces positive high-angle-of-attack loading: lift is positive and drag opposes the relative wind.
• Negative low angle of attack: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a pullout at the wing's highest angle of attack produces positive high-angle-of-attack loading: lift is positive and drag opposes the relative wind.
• Negative high angle of attack: It does not match the condition or structural role described; a pullout at the wing's highest angle of attack produces positive high-angle-of-attack loading: lift is positive and drag opposes the relative wind.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
The negative conditions reverse the normal lift direction; low-angle conditions do not describe the stated high-AoA pullout.

💡 Memory Hook:
Pullout + high AoA ? positive load.

🎯 Board Tip:
Identify both the load sign and angle-of-attack condition.

questions.question: This condition occur s at the diving speed limit of the airplane, it may occur in an intentional maneuver producing negative load factor or negative gust condition.
choices: Positive hi gh angle of attack 3 6

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Negative high angle of attack: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the described diving-speed case with negative load factor or negative gust corresponds to negative low angle of attack in the supplied key.
• Positive low angle of attack: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the described diving-speed case with negative load factor or negative gust corresponds to negative low angle of attack in the supplied key.
• Positive hi gh angle of attack 3 6: It does not match the condition or structural role described; the described diving-speed case with negative load factor or negative gust corresponds to negative low angle of attack in the supplied key.

Positive conditions have upward lift loading; negative high-AoA is not the stated diving-speed case.

💡 Memory Hook:
Negative load at dive speed ? negative low AoA.

🎯 Board Tip:
Match the sign of the lift/load to the flight condition.

questions.question: A 6,300 lb airplane is in a steady glide with flight path at an angle of 20 O below the horizontal. What is the LIFT and DRAG of the airplane
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: L = 5920 lb, D = 2155 lb. In a steady glide at 20? below horizontal, lift balances the perpendicular weight component and drag balances the along-path component: L = W cos 20? ? 5,920 lb; D = W sin 20? ? 2,155 lb.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• L = 5155 lb, D = 2920 lb: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in a steady glide at 20? below horizontal, lift balances the perpendicular weight component and drag balances the along-path component: l = w cos 20? ? 5,920 lb; d = w sin 20? ? 2,155 lb.
• L = 6120 lb, D = 3250 lb: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in a steady glide at 20? below horizontal, lift balances the perpendicular weight component and drag balances the along-path component: l = w cos 20? ? 5,920 lb; d = w sin 20? ? 2,155 lb.
• L = 5209 lb, D = 2551 lb: It does not match the condition or structural role described; in a steady glide at 20? below horizontal, lift balances the perpendicular weight component and drag balances the along-path component: l = w cos 20? ? 5,920 lb; d = w sin 20? ? 2,155 lb.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Interchanging sine and cosine swaps the larger perpendicular component and smaller along-path component; the total force must still balance the 6,300-lb weight.

💡 Memory Hook:
Lift uses cosine of glide angle; drag uses sine.

🎯 Board Tip:
Resolve weight parallel and perpendicular to the flight path.

questions.question: When a load is applied to a member normal to its axis and the member is held fixed at another sectio n, at any section between the load and reaction the particles on one side of the section tend to move in a transve rse direction with respect to the other side; that is, they tend to slide by each other. This set up internal stresses in the member called:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Shear stress. Shear stress is associated with adjacent portions of a member tending to slide transversely relative to one another.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Bending stress: It does not match the condition or structural role described; shear stress is associated with adjacent portions of a member tending to slide transversely relative to one another.
• Torsional stress: It does not match the condition or structural role described; shear stress is associated with adjacent portions of a member tending to slide transversely relative to one another.
• Tensile stress: It does not match the condition or structural role described; shear stress is associated with adjacent portions of a member tending to slide transversely relative to one another.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Bending causes curvature; torsion causes twist; direct compression acts along the member rather than across a section.

💡 Memory Hook:
Shear = sliding tendency across a section.

🎯 Board Tip:
Distinguish transverse shear from axial stress and torsional shear.

questions.question: During climb, the airplane accelerates at 48 ft/s 2 . If the weight of the airplane i s 3,800 lb, what is the load factor
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 2.5. For upward acceleration, the load factor is (g+a)/g = (32.2+48)/32.2 ? 2.5.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• 1.27: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for upward acceleration, the load factor is (g+a)/g = (32.
• 2.44: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for upward acceleration, the load factor is (g+a)/g = (32.
• 1.5: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for upward acceleration, the load factor is (g+a)/g = (32.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
Using a/g alone omits the force needed to support weight; dividing by the wrong acceleration component changes the factor.

💡 Memory Hook:
Upward acceleration: n = 1 + a/g.

🎯 Board Tip:
Include gravity when converting vertical acceleration to load factor.

questions.question: If the rivet shown in Fig. C (see page 6 ) has a shank diameter of 2.50 mm, what is the average stress in a section of the rivet between the two pieces of sheet at the given load

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• 153 Pa: It does not match the condition or structural role described; average direct shear stress is force divided by the rivet cross-sectional area.
• 153 KPa: It does not match the condition or structural role described; average direct shear stress is force divided by the rivet cross-sectional area.
• 15.3 MPa: It does not match the condition or structural role described; average direct shear stress is force divided by the rivet cross-sectional area.

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
The alternatives do not match the keyed load-over-area result for the section between the sheets.

💡 Memory Hook:
Rivet shear stress = transmitted force / shear-plane area.

🎯 Board Tip:
Check whether the rivet is in single or double shear from the figure.

questions.question: A propeller shaft, 4 ft long and 1.5 inches diameter is subjected to a torque of 390 ft - lb. What is the deflection angle if the modulus of rigidity is 11x10 6 lb/in 2

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• 0.47 degrees: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for a circular shaft, the twist angle follows ? = tl/(jg).
• 14.7 degrees: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for a circular shaft, the twist angle follows ? = tl/(jg).
• 4.7 degrees: It does not match the condition or structural role described; for a circular shaft, the twist angle follows ? = tl/(jg).

Differentiate Similar Concepts:
The remaining options are not the twist from the stated torsion relation and geometry.

Longer shaft or greater torque increases twist; larger J or G reduces it.
